title: Karun Nair Walks Out of South Zone Duleep Trophy Camp, Scores Defiant Century
excerpt: After being overlooked for both the semi-final and final, the veteran Karnataka batter left the squad and smashed 104 for KSCA Secretary XI, calling his exclusion "inexplicable."
body:
• Karun Nair left the South Zone squad during the Duleep Trophy final after being dropped for a second consecutive match, scoring 104 in a KSCA tournament in Bengaluru.
  • South Zone coach Vikram Verma cited "personal reasons" for Nair's departure, but the batter's X post calling his exclusion "inexplicable" told a different story.
  • Nair, who scored 699 runs in the 2025-26 Ranji season, was replaced by Devdutt Padikkal in the team's combination for the final against East Zone.
  • The controversy has reignited debate over selection transparency in Indian domestic cricket.

The Walkout

Karun Nair was at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on Saturday, training with his South Zone teammates on the eve of the Duleep Trophy final against East Zone. By Sunday evening, he was on a flight back to Bengaluru.

The 34-year-old, who has played 10 Tests for India, learned he had been left out of the playing XI for a second straight match — first the semi-final against North Zone, now the final. He emailed the team management seeking permission to leave, citing personal reasons, and departed.

On Monday, Nair turned up at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium — not as a spectator, but as a player. Representing KSCA Secretary XI against Chhattisgarh in the Dr K Thimmappaiah Memorial Tournament, he scored 104 off 183 balls, striking 12 fours and a six in a measured, defiant innings.

A Social Media Statement

The real fireworks came after stumps. A journalist on X described Nair's exclusion as "inexplicable." Nair quote-tweeted the post with a pointed reply: "Inexplicable would be an understatement," accompanied by a laughing emoji.

The post directly contradicted the official line from South Zone coach Vikram Verma, who told reporters in Chennai that Nair had left for "personal and family reasons."

"We went with a good combination because every team has two left-arm spinners. So we thought a left-hand batter in the middle order would give us a chance to dominate them."

— Vikram Verma, South Zone coach

The Selection Rationale

Verma explained that the arrival of an in-form Devdutt Padikkal for the final necessitated a change in the batting lineup. In the semi-final against North Zone, the team had given a chance to youngster Kodimela Himateja in the middle order. For the final, Padikkal — a left-hander — was slotted in to counter East Zone's twin left-arm spin attack.

Shaik Rasheed, who scored a duck and just one run across two innings in the semi-final, retained his place ahead of Nair. The decision raised eyebrows, particularly given Nair's prolific 2025-26 Ranji Trophy campaign where he amassed 699 runs for Karnataka.

Meanwhile, the final itself saw East Zone dominate with a massive first-innings total exceeding 700, led by captain Ishan Kishan's extraordinary 270 — only deepening questions about whether South Zone's combination could have benefited from Nair's experience.

A Pattern of Overlooking

Nair's case is not an isolated incident. The batter, best known for his unbeaten 303 against England in 2016, has been one of the most consistent run-scorers in Indian domestic cricket for several seasons. Despite his prolific output, a return to the India squad has remained elusive.

The Duleep Trophy, India's premier zonal red-ball competition, has traditionally served as a proving ground for Test selection. Being dropped from the squad — rather than just the playing XI — during such a high-profile fixture carries significant weight in selection discussions.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian cricket fans worldwide, the episode touches a nerve about merit-based selection, a topic that consistently generates passionate debate in diaspora communities. The Duleep Trophy's role as a feeder to the national Test side means these decisions have implications for who represents India in the longest format of the game.

As the Indian cricket season builds toward the next cycle of Test assignments, Nair's century on the same day he was snubbed will linger in the conversation — a statement made not through words, but through runs.
